intro: Every sport needs a room and someone in charge of it. In the late 1800s and early 1900s, American cities built many kinds of sports rooms. There were boxing clubs, YMCA gyms, settlement house gyms, park field houses, ballrooms and school gyms. Each room had its own owners, its own rules and its own crowd.

This unit follows two sports through those rooms. Boxing moved from secret fields to licensed arenas, and newspapers and radio made its fights national news. Yet Illinois school leagues never took it in. Basketball began in a YMCA in 1891 and spread through Ys, settlement houses, parks, ballrooms and school tournaments. Along the way, many people were shut out by race or sex, and you will learn the dates when doors opened.

By the end, you will be able to name the groups that ran each room, from the YMCA and Hull-House to the IHSA and state athletic commissions. You will be able to explain why a fight could fill the front page while the school board said no. You will also be able to trace Chicago's part in this story with real dates.
bigQuestion: Who decided which games belonged in the school gym, and which stayed in the club, the park and the newspaper?

timeline.t: Boxing is added to the ancient Olympic Games, according to Greek writers
Jack Broughton posts the oldest known boxing rules in London
The Queensberry Rules require gloves and three-minute rounds
Jane Addams and Ellen Gates Starr open Hull-House in Chicago
James Naismith invents basketball at the YMCA school in Springfield
Chicago opens ten neighborhood parks with field houses
Jack Johnson wins the heavyweight title; the IHSA holds its first boys basketball tournament
The Wabash Avenue YMCA opens for Black Chicagoans
Dempsey and Tunney fight at Soldier Field as millions listen on radio
Joe Louis wins the title at Comiskey Park; the NBL forms; IHSA crowns first wrestling champions
The first basketball game is shown on television
The NCAA holds its last college boxing championship

test.q: What did the Queensberry Rules of 1867 require?
test.why: The 1867 code required gloves and set rounds at three minutes.

test.q: Why were many big fights of the 1800s held in secret places?
choices: Prizefighting was illegal in most states.
test.why: Most states banned prizefighting, so promoters hid fight locations.

test.q: What did New York's Walker Law of 1920 do?
choices: created a state athletic commission to license boxing
test.why: The Walker Law set up the New York State Athletic Commission.

test.q: Which boxer was kept from a title fight by John L. Sullivan's color line?
test.why: Sullivan refused to fight Black challengers, which shut out Peter Jackson.

test.q: What did Congress ban in 1912, after Jack Johnson's win in Reno?
choices: shipping prizefight films across state lines
test.why: The 1912 law barred moving fight films between states.

test.q: Which fight was held at Soldier Field in Chicago in 1927?
test.why: The Long Count fight between Dempsey and Tunney drew more than 100,000 people to Soldier Field.

test.q: Who ran amateur boxing tournaments called the Golden Gloves?
choices: newspapers such as the Chicago Tribune
test.why: Newspapers, including the Tribune and the New York Daily News, ran Golden Gloves tournaments.

test.q: Which combat sport did the IHSA crown champions in, starting in 1937?
test.why: The IHSA's first boys wrestling champions came in 1937; it never held boxing championships.

choices: at a YMCA training school in Springfield, Massachusetts
test.why: Naismith created the game at the YMCA school in Springfield.

test.q: Why did Chicago build the Wabash Avenue YMCA?
choices: to give Black Chicagoans a Y when many Ys were segregated
test.why: The Wabash Avenue Y opened in 1913 for Black residents shut out of many Ys.

test.q: How did a settlement house like Hull-House work?
choices: Reformers lived in the neighborhood and ran classes and clubs.
test.why: Settlement workers lived among their neighbors and ran programs, including a gym.

test.q: What did Chicago's 1905 neighborhood parks include?
choices: field houses with gyms and clubrooms
test.why: Each of the ten 1905 parks had a field house.

test.q: Where did the Harlem Globetrotters begin?
test.why: The team grew out of South Side Chicago in the late 1920s.

test.q: Which two leagues merged in 1949 to form the NBA?
choices: the NBL and the Basketball Association of America
the Golden Gloves and the NBL
test.why: The NBL and BAA joined in 1949 as the National Basketball Association.

test.q: Which statement about women in these sports is correct?
choices: The IHSA held girls basketball finals in 1908.
Girls wrestling had IHSA state finals in 1937.
Women's boxing entered the Olympics in 2012.
test.why: Women's Olympic boxing began in London in 2012; IHSA girls wrestling finals began in the 2021–22 season.

write.prompt: Why did Illinois school leagues take in basketball but keep boxing out? Argue from at least three dated records in this unit, such as the 1908 IHSA tournament, the 1920 Walker Law, the 1937 IHSA wrestling championship or the end of NCAA boxing after 1960.
tips: Name each record or law you use and give its date.
Say who ran each room: a school league, a state board, a newspaper, a church or a club.
Compare the two sports side by side instead of only describing one.
Use unit words such as amateur, promoter, athletic commission and field house.
Say who was shut out of each room and when that changed.
